criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs has a deferred request (channel from `ask --later`) in state proposed whose latest reading passes the reading checks. The drain runs it and reports it as passed. Check with `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.
criteria.evidence: I ran the command: 175 passed. `a_proposed_deferred_request_with_a_passing_stored_reading_runs_without_a_second_reading` queues a request the way `ask --later` does and reads it with `go`. It then checks that the drain lands it with outcome "passed" and does not read it again. The test's own comment says this case already worked before the change, so it guards against regression. The behavior that is actually new has its own tests, which also report "passed": `a_proposed_deferred_request_with_no_stored_reading_is_read_and_run_by_the_batch` and `..._without_acceptance_words_...`. In these, a proposed request with no stored reading is read by the batch and run.

criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs has a request re-read with a changed scope after a settings change. The drain does not run it, reports outcome `needs accepting`, counts no failure, and does not stop the batch. Check with `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.
criteria.evidence: The new test `a_reread_whose_scope_changed_still_waits_for_a_person_in_every_batch` passes. In batch 1 the outcome is "needs accepting", nothing lands and there is no second attempt. In batch 2 the request is not queued, not read and not dispatched. A person's `go` still dispatches it. The updated `a_reread_whose_scope_changed_is_left_for_a_person_and_is_not_a_failure` checks the outcome, the reason and the note. Both of these batches hold only one item, so neither new test shows a second item running afterwards. That part is shown by the existing `a_run_that_needs_accepting_leaves_the_item_queued_without_a_failure`, which also passed. That test uses stub steps (an item after a needs-accepting item still lands), and the change does not touch that code path.

criteria.criterion: A test shows a proposed deferred request whose latest reading fails a reading check is not run by the batch. Another test shows a mixed run of proposed and queued items goes in priority order, with the urgent one before the lower priority one. Check with `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.
criteria.evidence: `a_proposed_request_whose_latest_reading_fails_a_reading_check_is_not_run_by_the_batch` passes. It first asserts that the seeded reading is refused by `check_reading_text`. The held request is then never started or dispatched, and a control request with a passing reading does run. `proposed_and_queued_requests_are_run_in_priority_order` passes. It mixes an urgent proposed request with no reading (the newest), a normal proposed request with a reading, and a low queued request. The start order is urgent, normal, low, and the urgent one lands first.

findings.summary: The fix may not cover the requests that prompted the job
findings.evidence: The producer found that a proposed request with a passing stored reading already ran. The real defect is in how a proposed request with no stored reading is handled. The CHANGELOG itself says it is not confirmed whether the 42 requests that never ran are of this kind. Records are absent from this snapshot, so I could not check either. The operator should confirm on the real repository, for example with `athena plan` after landing.

findings.summary: The new changed-scope test does not show the batch going on to a next item
findings.evidence: Each batch in this test holds only the one held request. So 'does not stop the batch' is shown only by the older stub test `a_run_that_needs_accepting_leaves_the_item_queued_without_a_failure`, not by a real-steps test. Adding a second queued request that lands after it would close this gap.

findings.summary: Held requests drop out of the plan and queue listing
findings.evidence: A proposed request whose reading fails a check, or a changed-scope re-read, is now left out of `queued_work`, which feeds both drain and plan. The only sign of it in batch output is the note in the batch that read it again. An operator might not see later that these requests are waiting for `athena go`. The docs say this, but the requests become less visible.

summary:
The change passes. The fix is in `steward::queued_work`. Before, every proposed request was marked as already read. Now a proposed request is handled by what its latest stored reading shows:
- It has a reading that passes the text-only reading checks: it runs without being read again.
- It has no stored reading: the batch reads it, then runs it or skips it.
- Its reading fails a check, or it was re-read after a settings change with a different scope: it waits for a person's `athena go` in every batch.

I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` (175 passed) and the steward unit tests (28 passed). The new tests cover the passing, no-reading, failing-check, changed-scope and priority-order cases. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. Only the four expected files changed, and the reading checks are not modified. The drain.rs docs and the CHANGELOG describe the rule and the root cause. Two minor findings remain:
- The producer did not confirm that the 42 stuck requests are of the kind this fixes. I could not check either, because records are absent from this snapshot.
- 'Does not stop the batch' for a changed-scope re-read rests on an older stub test, not on the new real-steps test.
